thought: His wife left him. Villagers thought he was mentally ill. He kept building anyway - and changed how millions of women live.
support: Arunachalam Muruganantham, a school dropout from Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, discovered that his newly married wife used rags instead of sanitary pads because branded pads were unaffordable. He spent years self-experimenting - including wearing a makeshift uterus device and testing pads himself - to understand absorbent materials, facing social ostracism along the way. He eventually invented a low-cost sanitary-pad-making machine that lets women's self-help groups manufacture pads locally at roughly a third of the commercial price. His machines have since been installed in over 1,300 villages across 23 Indian states. He received the Padma Shri in 2016 and was named to TIME's 100 Most Influential People in 2014.
